docket.challenge_claim: The unit registers a closure signal that its own close does not carry: the closing verse carries 0 neum tokens, and the 2 tokens inside the span both sit mid-verse, so the declared signal has nothing in this span's bytes to rest on.
docket.grounds: The byte facts hold exactly. The close reads וְשִׁלַּמְתִּ֥י לָהֶ֛ם כְּפָעֳלָ֖ם וּכְמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Jer.25.14, byte tier) and carries none of the formula -- the 162-verse inventory does not list it -- and the two in-span tokens at 25:9 and 25:12 both sit mid-verse and neither closes anything. What the framing overstates is that the signal has nothing to rest on. It rests on the front seam one verse before the span: 25:7 carries נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.25.7, byte tier) and 25:8 opens verse-initially on לָכֵ֕ן כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת (oshb:Jer.25.8, byte tier), a fresh tier-1 onset -- which is precisely the condition under which the ruled treatment lets that formula do closure work, and it is the pairing the boundary rationale itself names. Corrected finding: not a baseless key but an unscoped one, reading as a claim about this unit's own close where the bytes give nothing. Severity holds at low.
docket.remedy: Either bind the closure key to the seam it rests on by qualifying it as a front-seam signal, or drop it and let the koh-amar onset key carry the seam alone; in boundary_rationale, state that the closing verse carries no closure formula, so the close rests on the recompense clause completing the sentence begun at 25:8. Cure test: every declared closure signal must be present in the verse it is claimed of -- the test the original failed was a closure key whose only support lies outside the span. For consolidation: this is a corpus_wide_orders candidate rather than a one-unit fix. Ten units declare that closure key and six of them end on a verse carrying none of the 162, and the signal-field contract does not say whether a key may name a device outside the unit's own span; one order should settle the scope question rather than six independent guesses.

B4-6.docket_item: CWO-5 policy ruling: may a declared closure-classed observed_substrate_signals key name a device outside the declaring unit's own span? Enumerate the declaring rows from the frozen corpus and rule ONE scope policy.
B4-6.grounds: DETERMINISTIC ENUMERATION (swept from SP/Jer/draft_rows_combined.jsonl, 276 rows; the swept object is the observed_substrate_signals key speech_formula.neum_closure, named before any digit): 10 declaring rows - P05-002 Jer.13.12-Jer.13.14, P05-013 Jer.15.5-Jer.15.9, P07-007 Jer.21.11-Jer.21.14, P08-001 Jer.23.1-Jer.23.8, P08-002 Jer.23.9-Jer.23.15, P08-004 Jer.23.23-Jer.23.32, P09-002 Jer.25.8-Jer.25.14, P09-004 Jer.25.30-Jer.25.33, P18-007 Jer.49.23-Jer.49.27, P18-024 Jer.50.31-Jer.50.32. Six of the ten close on a verse carrying no neum token: P08-001 (MT 23:8), P08-002 (MT 23:15), P09-002 (MT 25:14), P09-004 (MT 25:33), P18-007 (MT 49:27), P18-024 (MT 50:32). The census matches the docket exactly. COUNT OBJECTS NAMED AND BOTH TESTED (E-05, and the test that corrected this ruling's own first pass): object A is the CONTIGUOUS two-word run neum-YHWH, skeleton tier, verse counts, MT keys - 162 verses, matching the inventory digit; object B is the bare neum TOKEN, skeleton substring, verse counts, MT keys - 169 verses, matching the inventory digit. Object B controls, because the key claims a token and the title-stack shapes are their own count objects. The two objects agree on which six rows fail at the close, so the consequence set is object-independent; they do NOT agree on where the support lies, and object A alone would have produced two false statements here. At MT 51:57 object A misses what object B finds, the melekh-signature stack standing between the two words. At MT 50:31 object A likewise misses the stack נְאֻם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָא֑וֹת (oshb:Jer.50.31, byte tier), which is one of the four adonai-stack sites - so P18-024, which object A shows as having no support anywhere in its span, in fact has support at its own opening verse. WHERE THE SUPPORT ACTUALLY LIES, per consequence row (neum-token verses inside each span under object B, MT keys): P08-001 MT 23:1, 23:2, 23:4, 23:5, 23:7; P08-002 MT 23:11, 23:12; P09-002 MT 25:9 and 25:12, both mid-verse and neither closing anything, with a further token one verse OUTSIDE and before the span at MT 25:7; P09-004 MT 25:31; P18-007 MT 49:26, the tsevaot stack נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת (oshb:Jer.49.26, byte tier), standing one verse before the row's own close; P18-024 MT 50:31, its opening verse. Out-of-span and off-close corroboration belongs in the same place. (4) Permitting qualified out-of-span keys would leave the field un-checkable by any span-scoped validator and would multiply disclosure text without adding evidence. The out-of-span arm of the policy is stated for completeness; no consequence row in this sweep turns on it.

consequence.spec: POLICY RULED (option (i), bind-or-drop, with the P09-002 cure test as the operative bar): a closure-classed observed_substrate_signals key is valid ONLY where the device it names stands in the DECLARING UNIT'S OWN CLOSING VERSE. In-span-but-not-closing support does not license it; out-of-span support NEVER licenses it. Where the key is dropped, the device is disclosed in prose with its verse ref and tier - never re-encoded under another key. CONSEQUENCE ROWS AND THE EDIT EACH TAKES (one edit per row): P08-001 Jer.23.1-Jer.23.8, P08-002 Jer.23.9-Jer.23.15, P09-002 Jer.25.8-Jer.25.14, P09-004 Jer.25.30-Jer.25.33, P18-007 Jer.49.23-Jer.49.27, P18-024 Jer.50.31-Jer.50.32 - each DROPS speech_formula.neum_closure from observed_substrate_signals, and each adds one sentence to boundary_rationale stating that its closing verse carries no closure formula and naming what actually closes the unit; where the token stands elsewhere in the span or before the front seam, that position is named in prose with its MT ref and byte tier and is NOT re-encoded as a key. P09-002's sentence states that the close rests on the recompense clause completing the sentence begun at 25:8, וְשִׁלַּמְתִּ֥י לָהֶ֛ם כְּפָעֳלָ֖ם וּכְמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Jer.25.14, byte tier), that its two in-span tokens at oshb:Jer.25.9 and oshb:Jer.25.12 stand mid-verse and close nothing, and that the token at oshb:Jer.25.7 stands outside the span and before its front seam. P18-024's sentence states that its only in-span token stands at its OPENING verse, oshb:Jer.50.31, in the adonai-stack shape - its own count object, four sites book-wide - and not at its close. P18-007's states that its token stands at oshb:Jer.49.26, one verse before the close, in the tsevaot stack shape. Where dropping the key leaves the row's driver set thinner, the dependent fields re-open with it: strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type and confidence are re-checked on each of the six. ROWS UNAFFECTED (key stands unchanged, device attested in the closing verse): P05-002, P05-013, P07-007, P08-004. CURE TEST each consequence row must pass: no closure-classed key survives in observed_substrate_signals whose named device is absent from the row's closing verse under the 169-verse neum-token object (skeleton tier, MT keys); and the prose sentence names the closing verse, states the absence, and names what closes the unit instead. SWEEP SCOPE (E-18): this order is carried to execution as its OWN sweep over observed_substrate_signals in draft_rows_combined.jsonl, scoped to the single key speech_formula.neum_closure (10 declarations). It is NOT folded into any row's fix and does NOT reach the sibling closure-classed keys, which are named here with their digits for a SEPARATE sweep under the same policy: speech_formula.neum_yhwh_closure, 6 declarations, 2 consequence rows (P02-004 Jer.4.14-Jer.4.18, close MT 4:18; P02-011 Jer.5.10-Jer.5.13, close MT 5:13); divine_title.neum_yhwh_closure, 6 declarations, 0 consequence rows. The three non-neum closure-classed keys (date_frame.narrative_date_closure, narrative_frame.speech_closure_transition, narrative_frame.summary_closure, 1 declaration each) name devices the neum objects cannot test and are outside both sweeps; they need their own named object before any digit.

current_row.boundary_rationale: “Therefore Yahweh of Armies says” (web:Jer.25.8) turns on לָכֵ֕ן כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת (oshb:Jer.25.8, byte tier) -- a pivot into a fresh declaration of consequence (the Babylonian invasion, the seventy-year servitude, and Babylon's own eventual reckoning) after the retrospective just closed, though the speaker is Yahweh in both the neum of 25:7 and the koh-amar here, so the seam rests more on the shift from recalling past warnings to pronouncing a dated sentence than on a clean change of who is speaking. The unit runs to 25:14, whose recompense clause closes the sentence begun at 25:8. Midway, the declaration states that Yahweh will bring on the land “even all that is written in this book” (web:Jer.25.13), spliced אֵ֤ת כָּל הַכָּתוּב֙ בַּסֵּ֣פֶר הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.25.13, byte tier; the verse's opening verb also carries a ketiv/qere note, consulted but not spliced here) -- a self-reference whose scope (this sermon alone, or a wider written collection) this tiling does not resolve, and the row is held at reduced confidence on that account rather than treated as a settled hinge.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping 25:1-14 as one row spanning the header through the recompense clause was considered: the divine voice does not clearly change between the retrospective and the declaration, so the pivot at 25:8 is a real but not decisive seam, and one fourteen-verse sermon unit would also be defensible.

docket.challenge_claim: The no-split ruling at 25:27 rests on an addressee the bytes contradict, and a second frame-command of the same shape stands undisclosed inside the span at 25:28.
docket.grounds: Both halves verified on bytes. 25:27 opens on וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֡ם (oshb:Jer.25.27, byte tier), a second-person-singular frame-command directed at the prophet, rendered “You shall tell them” (web:Jer.25.27); the forms addressed to the nations are the plurals inside the quoted speech it introduces, שְׁת֤וּ וְשִׁכְרוּ֙ וּקְי֔וּ וְנִפְל֖וּ (oshb:Jer.25.27, byte tier). Calling that verse a discourse imperative addressed to the nations collapses the outer frame into its own quoted speech, and the rejected alternative's stated ground -- that the addressee stays the same nations already compelled to drink -- is the part the bytes contest. That is where it bites: a rejected alternative is where the replacement warrant has to hold. The second half holds too. The same frame-command stands again inside the span at וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם (oshb:Jer.25.28, byte tier), unmentioned, so the span carries two rival command seams where the prose weighs one (sweep: 18 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, three of them consecutive here at 25:27, 25:28 and 25:30). The one-unit outcome is not overturned -- command, performance and enforcement still hold together on the ruled symbolic-act rule -- and the closing verse carries a genuine postpositive closure device the unit passes over, נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת (oshb:Jer.25.29, byte tier; sweep: 4 verses at skeleton tier). Medium is proportionate: prose and rejected-alternative repair, no boundary change.
docket.remedy: In boundary_rationale, recut the 25:27 sentence so the frame-command is described as addressed to the prophet and the drinking imperatives as the nations' address inside the quoted speech. In strongest_rejected_alternative, replace the addressee ground with the command-and-performance ground that actually carries the one-unit reading, and name the second frame-command at 25:28 as a further rival set aside. In device_notes, record the verse-final closure formula at 25:29 as the close's own corroboration, with its digit and tier. Cure test: every command in the span is read against its verbal form and its addressee before the prose asserts either -- the test the original failed was assigning a second-person-singular frame-command to the plural audience of the speech it introduces.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A private commission opens the row: “Take this cup of the wine of wrath from my hand” (web:Jer.25.15), spliced קַ֠ח אֶת כּ֨וֹס הַיַּ֧יִן הַחֵמָ֛ה הַזֹּ֖את מִיָּדִ֑י (oshb:Jer.25.15, byte tier) -- Yahweh, the God of Israel, addressing Jeremiah directly (“to me”), a scene shift from the dated declaration just closed. Jeremiah's own report of compliance follows, “Then I took the cup at Yahweh’s hand” (web:Jer.25.17), rendering וָאֶקַּ֥ח אֶת הַכּ֖וֹס מִיַּ֣ד יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.25.17, byte tier), and the roster of nations made to drink (25:18-26) runs into a command that keeps the same audience, “You shall tell them, ‘Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel says…” (web:Jer.25.27), spliced וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֡ם כֹּֽה אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Jer.25.27, byte tier) -- a discourse imperative addressed to the nations already given the cup rather than a new audience, so the row treats it as the act's own enforcement clause rather than a fresh unit. The whole complex closes at 25:29's declaration that Yahweh is calling for a sword against the earth. Whether this cup vision anticipates the later nations material or stands as this sermon's own close is left open here, and the row is held at reduced confidence on that account.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the row at 25:27, where a fresh command opens, was considered: the imperative shape is real, but the addressee stays the same nations already compelled to drink, so this tiling keeps the command, the performance, and the enforcement clause together as one enacted sign rather than opening a new row on the imperative alone.

Jer.25.14, just before this row, carries a setumah; within the span, Jer.25.27 carries a further setumah (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets) -- texture, not a driver of this boundary.

docket.challenge_claim: The seam device is asserted through the English alone and labelled with a form-class the pointed bytes do not carry, while the decisive byte fact for this seam (a single-site construction) goes unused.
docket.grounds: The evidence half is right and stands. The device that opens the unit, וְאַתָּה֙ תִּנָּבֵ֣א אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם (oshb:Jer.25.30, byte tier), verse-initial, is nowhere spliced -- both Hebrew splices in the rationale are the poem's content at 25:30b and 25:31 -- so the seam warrant carries no original-language quotation, which a boundary-relevant claim requires. The distinguishing digit does go unused: that verse-initial construction is a single site in the book (sweep: 1 verse at skeleton tier), while the frame-command following it in the same verse is an 18-verse shape standing uncut at 25:27 and 25:28. The label half is over-framed. The verb is prefix-conjugation, the same form standing under a negative at לֹ֤א תִנָּבֵא֙ (oshb:Jer.11.21, byte tier) and appearing in 6 verses at skeleton tier, so 'imperative' is not a morphological reading the bytes supply -- but the phrase used is the ruled name of a seam class rather than a bare form assertion, and the command force is byte-supported by the fronted second-person pronoun, by the frame-command that follows in the same verse, and by both witnesses' rendering. Corrected finding: an unspliced seam warrant and an unqualified form word, not a wrong seam; low. Two further defects neither item reaches. The unit declares no signal for its own stated driver while declaring the two devices it expressly refuses to cut on, and the taxonomy already carries a discourse-imperative onset key in use elsewhere in the corpus. And the declared closure key fails here in the same way it fails one unit earlier: the close at 25:33 carries none of the 162 neum verses, and the one verse-final instance in the span, at 25:31, does not close the unit.
docket.remedy: In boundary_rationale, splice the verse-initial seam construction from 25:30 with its oshb ref and tier named, and either qualify the form word -- command force carried by the fronted pronoun and the following frame-command, not by an imperative form -- or drop the form word; add the single-site digit (sweep: 1 verse at skeleton tier) beside it and state that the 18-verse frame-command shape in the same verse is not the discriminator. In observed_substrate_signals, add a key for the discourse-frame onset the rationale names as the driver, and remove or re-scope the closure key, whose device is absent from the closing verse. Cure test: every device the rationale names as a seam driver appears as a splice with its tier and as a declared signal, and every declared closure signal is present in the verse it is claimed of -- the tests the original failed were an English-only seam warrant and a driver with no signal entry.

(2) observed_substrate_signals is a record of the declaring row's own observed substrate and a dependent field of its drivers; a signal that stands outside the span is not this row's substrate at all. (3) The campaign already settles the same architecture for a weaker layer: parashah keys are BARRED from the field and their corroboration is carried in prose only. Out-of-span and off-close corroboration belongs in the same place. (4) Permitting qualified out-of-span keys would leave the field un-checkable by any span-scoped validator and would multiply disclosure text without adding evidence. The out-of-span arm of the policy is stated for completeness; no consequence row in this sweep turns on it.

consequence.spec: POLICY RULED (option (i), bind-or-drop, with the P09-002 cure test as the operative bar): a closure-classed observed_substrate_signals key is valid ONLY where the device it names stands in the DECLARING UNIT'S OWN CLOSING VERSE. In-span-but-not-closing support does not license it; out-of-span support NEVER licenses it. Where the key is dropped, the device is disclosed in prose with its verse ref and tier - never re-encoded under another key. CONSEQUENCE ROWS AND THE EDIT EACH TAKES (one edit per row): P08-001 Jer.23.1-Jer.23.8, P08-002 Jer.23.9-Jer.23.15, P09-002 Jer.25.8-Jer.25.14, P09-004 Jer.25.30-Jer.25.33, P18-007 Jer.49.23-Jer.49.27, P18-024 Jer.50.31-Jer.50.32 - each DROPS speech_formula.neum_closure from observed_substrate_signals, and each adds one sentence to boundary_rationale stating that its closing verse carries no closure formula and naming what actually closes the unit; where the token stands elsewhere in the span or before the front seam, that position is named in prose with its MT ref and byte tier and is NOT re-encoded as a key. P09-002's sentence states that the close rests on the recompense clause completing the sentence begun at 25:8, וְשִׁלַּמְתִּ֥י לָהֶ֛ם כְּפָעֳלָ֖ם וּכְמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Jer.25.14, byte tier), that its two in-span tokens at oshb:Jer.25.9 and oshb:Jer.25.12 stand mid-verse and close nothing, and that the token at oshb:Jer.25.7 stands outside the span and before its front seam. P18-024's sentence states that its only in-span token stands at its OPENING verse, oshb:Jer.50.31, in the adonai-stack shape - its own count object, four sites book-wide - and not at its close. P18-007's states that its token stands at oshb:Jer.49.26, one verse before the close, in the tsevaot stack shape. Where dropping the key leaves the row's driver set thinner, the dependent fields re-open with it: strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type and confidence are re-checked on each of the six. ROWS UNAFFECTED (key stands unchanged, device attested in the closing verse): P05-002, P05-013, P07-007, P08-004. CURE TEST each consequence row must pass: no closure-classed key survives in observed_substrate_signals whose named device is absent from the row's closing verse under the 169-verse neum-token object (skeleton tier, MT keys); and the prose sentence names the closing verse, states the absence, and names what closes the unit instead. SWEEP SCOPE (E-18): this order is carried to execution as its OWN sweep over observed_substrate_signals in draft_rows_combined.jsonl, scoped to the single key speech_formula.neum_closure (10 declarations). It is NOT folded into any row's fix and does NOT reach the sibling closure-classed keys, which are named here with their digits for a SEPARATE sweep under the same policy: speech_formula.neum_yhwh_closure, 6 declarations, 2 consequence rows (P02-004 Jer.4.14-Jer.4.18, close MT 4:18; P02-011 Jer.5.10-Jer.5.13, close MT 5:13); divine_title.neum_yhwh_closure, 6 declarations, 0 consequence rows. The three non-neum closure-classed keys (date_frame.narrative_date_closure, narrative_frame.speech_closure_transition, narrative_frame.summary_closure, 1 declaration each) name devices the neum objects cannot test and are outside both sweeps; they need their own named object before any digit.

docket.challenge_claim: One item: the opening edge is warranted but the closing edge at 26:6 has no warrant at all, the participant and scene shift opening immediately after being neither cited nor discussed. The other: the unit is cut exactly where its commissioned words are performed and quoted back, with neither the straddling material nor the resulting risk disclosed while confidence stands at high with the frontier flag unset, and the site is named in prose by the other byform.
docket.grounds: Related but distinct items on one seam; both principal charges hold. The evidence list and the rationale both stop at 26:6, no reference to 26:7 appears in either, and the closing sentence argues only the unit's internal cohesion -- so the close is unwarranted on its face. The straddle is byte-true in two devices. The threat in the closing verse, וְנָתַתִּ֛י אֶת הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּ֖ה כְּשִׁלֹ֑ה (oshb:Jer.26.6, byte tier), returns as the charge laid against the prophet at כְּשִׁלוֹ֙ יִֽהְיֶה֙ הַבַּ֣יִת הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.9, byte tier): the house phrase is a narrow object (sweep: 6 verses at skeleton tier, half of them in this chapter) and the Shiloh element is per-site, the closing verse's spelling a single site in the book (sweep: 1 verse) against nine for the spelling used across the cut. And the command אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּיתִ֖יךָ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.26.2, byte tier) is reported carried out at אֵ֣ת כָּל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.8, byte tier). Neither device is disclosed, and the calibration is high with the frontier flag unset. The byform sub-item does not stand: the construction's campaign name covers all three sites in two spellings, and the site's own attested plene form בְּרֵאשִׁ֗ית מַמְלְכ֛וּת (oshb:Jer.26.1, byte tier) is spliced byte-true in the very sentence that uses the class name, against בְּרֵאשִׁ֗ית מַמְלֶ֛כֶת (oshb:Jer.27.1, byte tier) at the other two (sweep: 1 verse and 2 verses at skeleton tier) -- no digit or form claim is left unattested, so there is nothing to cure there. Medium on the principal charges. This seam is shared with the unit opening at 26:7, and the two cures are one edit.
docket.remedy: Paired seam edit, made once for both sides. In boundary_rationale, add the closing-edge warrant: name the participant and scene change at 26:7 as the ruled seam class that stops this unit at 26:6, and add web:Jer.26.7 to boundary_evidence_refs. In device_notes, disclose the two straddling devices -- the threat quoted back at 26:9 with the per-site Shiloh spellings and their digits, and the command reported performed at 26:8 -- and state that they are weighed as continuity and do not overturn the participant seam. Then set confidence to medium and frontier_flag_considered to true. No byform edit is required. Cure test: the closing seam carries a named tier-1 warrant plus a reference to the verse that opens after it, and every device crossing the seam is disclosed with its count and tier -- the tests the original failed were a warrantless close and an undisclosed command-and-quotation straddle at high confidence.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A reign-dated bereshit-mamlekhet header opens the row: “In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came from Yahweh” (web:Jer.26.1), spliced בְּרֵאשִׁ֗ית מַמְלְכ֛וּת יְהוֹיָקִ֥ים בֶּן יֹאשִׁיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה הָיָה֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.1, byte tier) -- distinct in shape from the cup oracle's own date-and-word-event opening just closed. Yahweh's private instruction to Jeremiah follows: “Stand in the court of Yahweh’s house” (web:Jer.26.2), rendering עֲמֹד֮ בַּחֲצַ֣ר בֵּית יְהוָה֒ (oshb:Jer.26.2, byte tier), commanding him to speak the full warning without omission, closing on the Shiloh threat, “I will make this house like Shiloh” (web:Jer.26.6), spliced וְנָתַתִּ֛י אֶת הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּ֖ה כְּשִׁלֹ֑ה (oshb:Jer.26.6, byte tier; the verse also carries a ketiv/qere note further on, on the demonstrative for the threatened city, consulted but not spliced here). The command and the content it dictates stay one unit because no scene change separates the header from the instruction it introduces.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating 26:1 as a bare header, separate from the instruction that follows, was considered and set aside: the command in 26:2-6 carries the row's substance, delivered in the same private scene the header opens.
current_row.literature_type_guess: reign-dated word-event notice commissioning the temple-court warning
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate

docket.challenge_claim: The front seam at 26:7 is argued as a clean turn to public narration while two byte-true devices inside the span reach back across it undisclosed, and the boundary is still rated high confidence; the Hebrew engagement offered for the seam is a verb shape that also opens the next seam, so it does not discriminate between the two cuts.
docket.grounds: The byte facts are right. The completion clause אֵ֣ת כָּל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.8, byte tier) reports the charge אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּיתִ֖יךָ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.26.2, byte tier) carried out; the threat is quoted back at כְּשִׁלוֹ֙ יִֽהְיֶה֙ הַבַּ֣יִת הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.9, byte tier) from וְנָתַתִּ֛י אֶת הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּ֖ה כְּשִׁלֹ֑ה (oshb:Jer.26.6, byte tier), the per-site spellings differing (sweep: 1 verse and 9 verses at skeleton tier); and the seam verb וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֛וּ (oshb:Jer.26.7, byte tier) recurs at וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֣וּ (oshb:Jer.26.10, byte tier), one of 7 verses at skeleton tier, so it does not by itself separate the two cuts. Two corrections lower the weight. The continuity relation is not wholly unstated: the rationale names this scene as the one where the preceding private instruction is carried out, so what is missing is the byte-level engagement -- no splice, no digit, no weighing -- rather than the relation itself. And the seam is not carried by the verb: the discriminator the unit states is the participant and scene change, a ruled tier-1 class evidenced by a byte-true splice at the seam verse, with the verb as corroboration. What remains is a disclosure gap plus calibration at high confidence on a boundary that does argue both its edges, the far edge through its rejected alternative. Refined to low.
docket.remedy: In device_notes, disclose the two devices reaching back over the front seam -- the completion clause answering the charge, and the threat quoted back with its per-site spellings and digits -- and state that they are weighed against the participant seam and do not overturn it. Set confidence to medium and frontier_flag_considered to true, or argue in boundary_rationale why high survives the disclosed anaphora. This is the same seam as the unit closing at 26:6: make the two disclosures as one paired edit so both sides agree. Cure test: every byte-true device crossing this seam appears once on each side of the pair with a digit and a tier -- the test the original failed was an English-only allusion to the command-and-performance relation carried at high confidence.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The narration turns external at 26:7: “The priests and the prophets and all the people heard Jeremiah” (web:Jer.26.7), spliced וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֛וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֥ים וְהַנְּבִאִ֖ים וְכָל הָעָ֑ם אֶֽת יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.26.7, byte tier) -- a scene shift from Yahweh's private instruction to the public temple-court scene where that instruction is carried out, third-person and crowd-facing rather than a private divine command. The seizure follows at once, rendered from וַיִּתְפְּשׂ֨וּ אֹת֜וֹ (oshb:Jer.26.8, byte tier), and the crowd's confrontation over why he prophesied runs through 26:9's closing notice that the people gathered around Jeremiah.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through 26:16's acquittal was considered: the seizure and the formal hearing belong to one ordeal, but the princes' arrival at 26:10 marks a fresh set of participants convening a distinct judicial scene, which this tiling opens as its own row.
current_row.literature_type_guess: narrated seizure scene following the delivered temple-court warning
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
current_row.device_notes: Jer.26.6, just before this row, carries a setumah (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets).

docket.challenge_claim: The closure argument rests on an untiered verbatim-class recurrence claim that the bytes contest: accusation and acquittal share a collocation but neither an order nor an accentuation.
docket.grounds: Verified. The accusation reads מִשְׁפַּט מָ֨וֶת֙ לָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.11, byte tier) and the verdict אֵין לָאִ֤ישׁ הַזֶּה֙ מִשְׁפַּט מָ֔וֶת (oshb:Jer.26.16, byte tier): the same four words, reordered around the negator, and each of the three accented words differently accented across the two verses -- so the recurrence is not byte-identical, and it is not a contiguous four-word run at skeleton tier either. What does recur is two two-word collocations, the death-sentence pair and the this-man pair, each confined to these two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses apiece at skeleton tier). The rationale's claim that the verdict answers the charge in the very words used to accuse is a recurrence claim carrying no tier label, which the standing rule requires at write time, and the exclusivity that would have sharpened it is available and unclaimed. The echo is real and the boundary is untouched; the defect is one of labelling. Low.
docket.remedy: In boundary_rationale, replace the very-words wording with a tier-labelled statement: the verdict reuses the accusation's death-sentence and this-man collocations, reordered around the negator, matching at skeleton tier and not at byte tier, each collocation confined to these two verses (sweep: 2 verses each). Cure test: no recurrence claim stands without its tier, and no word-order identity is implied where the bytes reorder -- the test the original failed was an unlabelled verbatim-class claim over a reordered pair.

current_row.boundary_rationale: New participants convene the row: “the princes of Judah heard these things” (web:Jer.26.10), spliced וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֣וּ שָׂרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.26.10, byte tier) -- the princes arriving from the king's house to take their seats at the new gate, a fresh judicial tableau distinct from the crowd's own confrontation just narrated. The priests and prophets lay a formal charge, “This man is worthy of death” (web:Jer.26.11), rendering מִשְׁפַּט מָ֨וֶת֙ לָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.11, byte tier), and Jeremiah's own defense (26:12-15) turns the verdict: “This man is not worthy of death” (web:Jer.26.16), spliced אֵין לָאִ֤ישׁ הַזֶּה֙ מִשְׁפַּט מָ֔וֶת (oshb:Jer.26.16, byte tier) -- the princes and the people answering the priests and prophets in the very words used to accuse him.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Running 26:10-19 together as one trial scene was considered: the princes' hearing and the elders' supporting testimony both serve the same proceeding, but the elders rising to speak at 26:17 introduce a new speaking party making its own self-contained argument, which this tiling opens as a separate row.
current_row.literature_type_guess: narrated temple-court hearing: formal accusation answered by Jeremiah's defense and the princes' acquittal
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate

docket.challenge_claim: Both original-language disclosures overstate what the bytes give: the ketiv/qere is reported one word too wide, and the plene Jerusalem contrast is drawn against a comparand that does not isolate the plene variable.
docket.grounds: Both arms are byte-true. MT 26:18 runs מיכיה מִיכָה֙ הַמּ֣וֹרַשְׁתִּ֔י (oshb:Jer.26.18, byte tier): the unpointed ketiv, then the pointed qere, then ordinary pointed text; the note inventory carries exactly one note at that verse, covering one word. The row names מִיכָה֙ הַמּ֣וֹרַשְׁתִּ֔י as the qere, which annexes an unnoted word into the apparatus. Second, the plene site is vav-prefixed, וִירוּשָׁלַ֨יִם֙ (oshb:Jer.26.18, byte tier), while the comparand offered from 25:18 is יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ (oshb:Jer.25.18, byte tier), unprefixed, so the pair varies the conjunction as well as the mater; a same-shape comparand stands in the bytes at וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:Jer.27.21, byte tier, also at oshb:Jer.27.20) (sweep: vav-prefixed defective spelling 6 verses; plene spelling 1 verse, this site). Two further defects at the same verse, raised by neither item: the seg inventory carries a paseq at MT 26:18, inside this span, and the row's disclosure sentence speaks only to parashah marks, so the span's seg-layer disclosure is incomplete (count-only, single-witness); and the gloss “Zion will be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem will become heaps” (web:Jer.26.18) is paired with a splice ending at וִירוּשָׁלַ֨יִם֙ that does not contain עִיִּ֣ים תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.18, byte tier), so quote and splice are not co-extensive. The seam at 26:17 and the medium_low calibration are untouched; severity is medium on the added findings, not on the challenge as framed, which sits at low.
docket.remedy: boundary_rationale: cut the qere report to the single word the note covers (ketiv מיכיה against qere מִיכָה֙), leaving הַמּ֣וֹרַשְׁתִּ֔י as ordinary text; replace the 25:18 comparand with the vav-prefixed defective spelling at oshb:Jer.27.20 or oshb:Jer.27.21 so the pair varies only the mater, each spelling carrying a digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit; re-cut the Zion/Jerusalem pairing so the English and the splice are co-extensive (extend the splice through עִיִּ֣ים תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה or shorten the quote to end at Jerusalem). boundary_evidence_refs: add oshb:Jer.27.20 / oshb:Jer.27.21 (and web: counterparts) for the new comparand and drop the 25:18 pair if it is no longer argued. device_notes: add the paseq at oshb:Jer.26.18 as count-only, single-witness. Tests the cure must pass: the qere sentence names exactly the one word the note carries; the spelling pair differs in one variable only; every English quote is byte-verbatim and co-extensive with its paired splice; and every verse argued in prose outside the span appears in boundary_evidence_refs.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A new speaking party rises within the same hearing: “Then certain of the elders of the land rose up, and spoke to all the assembly” (web:Jer.26.17) opens the row, introducing witnesses distinct from the princes, priests, and prophets already heard. Their precedent-citation names the source directly: “Micah the Morashtite prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah” (web:Jer.26.18), spliced מִיכָה֙ הַמּ֣וֹרַשְׁתִּ֔י הָיָ֣ה נִבָּ֔א (oshb:Jer.26.18, byte tier) -- the ketiv spells the prophet's name מיכיה, read here against the qere מִיכָה֙ הַמּ֣וֹרַשְׁתִּ֔י that this splice follows, consulted but not further marked. The quoted oracle itself reads “Zion will be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem will become heaps” (web:Jer.26.18), rendering צִיּ֞וֹן שָׂדֶ֤ה תֵֽחָרֵשׁ֙ וִירוּשָׁלַ֨יִם֙ (oshb:Jer.26.18, byte tier) -- Jerusalem spelled plene here, וִירוּשָׁלַ֨יִם֙, against the defective יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ (oshb:Jer.25.18, byte tier). The elders draw the historical conclusion at 26:19: Hezekiah did not put Micah to death, so the present assembly should not put Jeremiah to death either. Whether this testimony belongs inside the same row as the princes' own hearing (26:10-16) or opens its own unit, as here, is a close call this tiling does not treat as settled.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding the elders' testimony into the princes' hearing as one scene (26:10-19) was considered: both serve the same acquittal, but the elders are a distinct participant group introduced by their own rising-and-speaking notice, which this tiling keeps as a separate row.
current_row.literature_type_guess: elders' precedent testimony citing Micah's Zion oracle to argue Jeremiah's acquittal
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate

docket.challenge_claim: Each of the row's two pivots turns on a particle it does not weigh: the opening coordinator is byte evidence for the reading the row rejects, and the closing adversative that carries the asserted contrast is left outside the splice while the English reaches wider than the splice does.
docket.grounds: The first arm is upheld and the second is real but mis-framed. Upheld: the row's own first word is the coordinator וְגַם (oshb:Jer.26.20, byte tier), which is the byte ground for reading 26:20-26:23 as continuing the elders' speech — the very reading the rationale sets aside with the assertion that the case stands on its own footing; a device sitting at the row's own opening seam argues continuity unless it is answered, and strongest_rejected_alternative answers a different rival (splitting off 26:24). Real but mis-framed: the adversative אַ֗ךְ (oshb:Jer.26.24, byte tier) is indeed outside the splice, which begins at יַ֚ד, and it is the one byte carrying the contrast the same sentence asserts — but the added charge that the English reaches wider is byte-false here: the paired quote “the hand of Ahikam the son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah” (web:Jer.26.24) also begins after the adversative, since the verse reads “But the hand of Ahikam” (web:Jer.26.24); gloss and splice are co-extensive and simply start one word late. That charge does land one verse-set earlier in the same row, unraised by either item: “There was also a man who prophesied in Yahweh’s name” (web:Jer.26.20) is paired with a splice ending at מִתְנַבֵּא֙ which does not contain בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.20, byte tier). Disclosure is otherwise correct: the petuchah at MT 26:24 is the only inventory entry across 26:20-26:24, with no segs and no notes there. The boundary is untouched.
